assets.prompt: Use case: style-transfer / game sprite atlas. Reference image 1 is the existing Bureau furniture to reinterpret as independent sprites; reference image 2 is the desired crisp, rich, natural pixel-art material treatment and three-quarter top-down RPG viewpoint. Create a genuinely transparent 2x2 ATLAS, FOUR isolated furniture assemblies only, with broad empty transparent gutters and equal cells. Upper-left: a warm oak boss desk with dark teal swivel chair tucked behind, small monitor, cream papers, blue desk lamp and a little succulent; desk front faces south/viewer, complete four legs. Upper-right: a distinct warm oak reception desk with teal chair behind, dark monitor, cream notebook, desk phone and pencil pot; same orientation. Lower-left: a tall narrow muted teal metal filing cabinet with drawers, cream label slots, a small stacked book and fern on top. Lower-right: a narrow two-seat teal upholstered waiting bench with warm wooden frame, viewed from front/south, one cream cushion, a terracotta planter with a leafy plant beside it. Match the same calm coastal office palette across all four. Intended native game sizes are approximately 128x88 for each desk, 40x86 for the cabinet, 84x56 for the bench. Use chunky controlled pixel clusters, broken highlights on warm wood, blue-green recessed shadows, 4-6 shades per material, selective dark outlines, readable material wear. Light consistently from upper-left. Camera is slightly top-down, orthographic, horizontal front edges, not diamond isometric. Keep each item entirely within its own cell, no item touches another cell. No background room, floor, curtain, walls, cast floor shadows, people, characters, UI, labels or readable words. True transparent alpha around the complete sprites. No photographic grain, painterly blur, smooth vectors or 3D render. Only the four pixel-art cutouts.

Use case: style-transfer / layered RPG prop atlas. Reference image 1 is the existing depot yard: preserve the identities of its remorque, workshop and potion trolley. Reference image 2 gives the rich crisp natural pixel-art style, compact three-quarter top-down objects, teal recesses and warm highlights. Output FOUR independent fully visible prop assemblies in a clean equal-cell 2x2 grid with genuinely transparent background and wide empty transparent gutters. UPPER LEFT: a small grey utility trailer/remorque, seen from its rear at a slight top-down angle, two rear doors with one partly open showing tidy garden tools, visible wheels and metal latch, warm wear on grey metal. UPPER RIGHT: a compact open maintenance workshop/hangar facade, pale grey corrugated roof with warm weathered frame and cream awning, a teal workbench, tools neatly hung on a back board, shelves and a coiled hose, with tiny vines at its side. Its front edge is horizontal and faces south. LOWER LEFT: a cleaner's wooden and teal potion trolley/counter, small wheels, red-heart-shaped fantasy healing flasks with glowing red liquid, a mop and bucket, no canopy, readable small storage shelves. LOWER RIGHT: a gardener's low outdoor storage rack with warm wood shelves, stacked terracotta pots, teal tool boxes, rolled hoses and two cream garden sacks. Light consistently from upper-left. Native target sizes around trailer 128x118, workshop 220x152, trolley 80x84, rack 108x86. Deliberate crisp stepped pixels, selective dark coloured outlines, 4-6 well chosen tones per material, pale highlights and cooler teal shadows, richer textured material clusters but no noise. Every whole prop isolated within its own equal grid cell, no cropping, no contact between cells. No yard, ground, floor, cast floor shadow, people, character, text, signs, logo or UI. Truly transparent alpha, no checkerboard baked in. No photographic texture, 3D render, gradients or antialiased vector art.

Use case: style-transfer, production pixel-art VEHICLE ATLAS for the existing coastal maintenance RPG. Replace the steel-coloured utility trailer direction in reference image 1 with a cheerful small fleet, maintaining that exact richly textured yet crisp game-art treatment. Reference image 2 sets the compact top-down three-quarter RPG perspective. Output THREE isolated whole vans in ONE horizontal row of THREE equal-width cells on genuinely transparent alpha. Each van must stay within its own third of the canvas with wide empty gutters. Same ground baseline, consistent top-down camera and upper-left warm sunlight, front edges horizontal, slight rear three-quarter view so rear cargo and one side are visible. LEFT: Matt's warm sunshine-yellow mid-size Renault-style work van (roughly a Jumpy/Trafic-sized gardener van), not a truck or trailer. Rounded compact cab, black bumper, grey tyres, rear cargo doors partly open. Gardening tools inside: green watering can, rake, spade, coiled green hose and folded work gloves; a small roof rack with a bundled ladder. No detached trailer. CENTER: Karine's smaller WHITE Renault Kangoo-style compact panel van, clearly different rounded Kangoo shape and short wheelbase. Rear door open showing a teal technician toolbox, cable reel, service cases and a wrench; modest dark teal work accents. RIGHT: Jojo's smaller WHITE Renault Kangoo-style compact panel van with cleaning supplies in its open rear: blue mop bucket, mop, folded cleaning cloths, small tidy red healing-flask case. It is a cleaner's work van, not an ambulance. Keep both Kangoo vans predominantly white; their cargo distinguishes them. A tiny simple diamond-shaped grille badge is okay, but no readable text or labels anywhere. Native targets approximately 128x112 pixels for the yellow van and 108x98 pixels for each white van. Every tyre, mirror, door and roof rack fits its own cell, with no overlapping assets or cropped parts. Crisp stepped silhouettes, deliberate pixel clusters, warm cream highlights, cool teal-grey recesses, controlled 4-6 tones per material, no photographic grain or smooth airbrush rendering. No people, floor, ground, cast floor shadow, background scene, UI, title or checkerboard. The output is ONLY the three full pixel-art vehicle cutouts on genuine transparency.

Use case: stylized-concept, production pixel-art vehicle cutouts. Match the attached maintenance-van atlas's compact three-quarter rear view, lighting, crisp pixel clusters, dark coloured edge treatment and perspective. Create ONLY TWO complete passenger vehicles, side by side in two clearly separated equal cells with generous transparent gutters, both standing on the same baseline. LEFT: a BLACK Renault Scénic compact family MPV, the familiar rounded five-door people-carrier silhouette, dark charcoal-black body with subtle cool grey-blue reflections, grey tyres, tail lamps and rear hatch closed, a small diamond Renault badge. RIGHT: a WHITE Volkswagen Polo compact five-door hatchback, recognisably shorter and lower than the Scénic, warm white body, dark glass, grey tyres, rear hatch closed and a small round VW badge. No cargo, roof racks, tools, people or extra cars. No readable license numbers, text or labels. Slight top-down three-quarter rear angle matching the attached van cutouts, all mirrors and tyres fully visible and inside their respective cells. Consistent upper-left daylight. Deliberate authentic pixel-art clusters and stepped highlights, controlled 4-6 shades per material, no smooth 3D rendering, photographic noise or airbrushing. Intended native game exports around 96x76 for the black Scénic and 86x68 for the white Polo; retain clear shape differences when small. TRUE transparent alpha around each isolated vehicle. No floor, cast ground shadow, scenery, border, checkerboard or UI. These are spare game assets for later use.

Use case: precise-object-edit / production pixel-art office prop atlas. Rework the office props from the reference into the NEW orientations below, preserving the warm oak, deep teal, careful pixel clusters and top-down three-quarter RPG camera. Output FOUR complete isolated furniture pieces in an equal 2x2 grid, genuinely transparent alpha, with wide transparent gutters, no floor and no ground shadow. UPPER LEFT: a SMALL WOODEN COMPUTER DESK whose LONG AXIS runs VERTICALLY north-to-south in the image, to stand along a room's LEFT/WEST wall. Its long left edge is the wall side; the working/user edge is on the RIGHT/EAST. Oak tabletop, one computer and keyboard oriented toward the RIGHT/east user, a small paper stack; NO chair and NO person. The silhouette must be narrow left-to-right and long top-to-bottom (roughly 58x94 native pixels), with short edges at the TOP and BOTTOM; do not draw a conventional wide horizontal front desk. UPPER RIGHT: a TALL WHITE STANDING RECEPTION COUNTER, long axis horizontal east-west, white vertical front panel facing south/viewer, waist-to-chest height, clean off-white top with subtly shaded edges. Put a computer on the RIGHT end, leaving the LEFT half of the work surface clear so a receptionist's head can remain visible behind it. This is an above-waist service counter, not a seated wooden desk. Native target about 112x80 including monitor. LOWER LEFT: a LARGE DEEP-TEAL SOFA for the LEFT/WEST wall, long axis VERTICAL north-to-south in the image. Backrest on the LEFT/WEST, open seat side on the RIGHT/EAST. Three seat cushions arranged one above another along the vertical axis, warm wood feet, a cream cushion near one end. It faces RIGHT/east, not toward the bottom of the image. Narrow and long silhouette about 60x104 native pixels. LOWER RIGHT: a LOW SQUARE WOODEN COFFEE TABLE, almost square tabletop in the top-down camera, four short feet, two overlapping magazines with colourful blue and terracotta covers and small page-edge marks, NO readable text. This table will sit to the RIGHT/east of the vertical sofa. Native target 46x44. Keep every item fully inside its cell, no item touches another cell. Consistent upper-left warm highlights and cool teal-grey recessed shading, crisp stepped outlines, discrete colour clusters and 4-6 tones per material. Match the attached game art quality, no painterly blur, no photographic grain, no smooth 3D shading. No room, walls, plants, chairs, people, extra furniture, UI, labels, floor, cast shadows or checkerboard background. Only the four transparent pixel-art props with the specified orientations.
